result: The authors developed a CLZ3 cell line for high-throughput screening of compounds affecting DSB repair pathway choice. The CLZ3 cell line was derived from D4a cells and contains a dual-reporter system that measures both HR and NHEJ efficiency simultaneously at the same chromosomal site, along with a doxycycline-inducible I-SceI expression system.
evaluation: Claims C1-C4 collectively establish the successful generation and validation of the CLZ3 screening platform. The derivation from D4a cells (C1, C2) is supported by citation, and functional validation showing doxycycline-induced I-SceI expression (C3) and resulting tdTomato+ and GFP+ cells (C4) is supported by experimental data in Figures 1C-E.

result: Through screening 722 small molecules from traditional Chinese medicine, the authors identified farrerol as a compound that promotes HR but has no effect on NHEJ. This effect was validated in multiple cell lines including CLZ3, HCA2-H15c, HCA2-I9a, and mouse ESCs.
evaluation: Claims C5-C10 describe the screening and initial validation of farrerol. The screening of 722 compounds (C5) and identification of farrerol (C6-C8) are supported by experimental data in Figure 1G. Validation in multiple cell lines (C9-C10) is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B, demonstrating reproducibility across different systems.

result: Farrerol promotes HR through stimulating the recruitment of RAD51 to DSB sites rather than by altering expression levels of HR-related factors or cell cycle distribution. Farrerol treatment resulted in increased RAD51 foci at 4 hr post-IR (6.5 and 6.1 vs 4.4 in control) and faster clearance at 16 hr post-IR (3.2 and 4.3 vs 6.4 in control).
evaluation: Claims C11-C18 and C66 establish the mechanism of farrerol action. Western blot data (C11, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) shows no changes in protein expression, cell cycle analysis (C13, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) shows no cell cycle effects, and immunofluorescence data (C15-C17, Figure 1—figure supplement 2E-F) demonstrates altered RAD51 recruitment kinetics. The mechanistic conclusion (C18, C66) is well-supported by this converging evidence.

result: Farrerol significantly suppressed SSA efficiency by 3.3-fold and 1.9-fold at concentrations of 5 μM and 10 μM respectively, while RS-1 had no effect on SSA. This suggests farrerol might help maintain genome integrity by avoiding aberrant recombination between repetitive sequences.
evaluation: Claims C19-C22 describe farrerol's effect on SSA. The lack of RAD51 involvement in SSA (C19) is supported by citations and confirmed experimentally with RS-1 (C20). Farrerol's suppression of SSA (C21) is supported by quantitative data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C. The speculation about genome integrity (C22) is a reasonable inference from the data, though it remains to be directly tested.

result: Farrerol significantly stimulated CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-in efficiency by ~2.0 fold at the AAVS1 locus in HEK 293FT cells at concentrations of 1 and 5 μM, with effects similar to RS-1 or SCR7 treatment. Farrerol showed no significant effect on cell proliferation, suggesting low toxicity.
evaluation: Claims C23-C27 demonstrate farrerol's application in genome editing. Knock-in efficiency data (C23-C24) is supported by Figures 2D-E and validated with an alternative donor vector (C27, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C). Cell proliferation data (C25-C26, Figure 2F) supports the low toxicity claim. The results are consistent across different experimental approaches.

result: Farrerol significantly promoted CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-in efficiency in mouse ESCs at multiple genomic loci: 2.8-fold at Actb (10 μM), 2.9-fold at Rosa26 (5 μM), and 2.0-fold at Sox2 (5 μM). In contrast, SCR7 and RS-1 had only mild effects at the Actb locus.
evaluation: Claims C28-C32 demonstrate farrerol's efficacy across multiple loci in mouse ESCs. Data for Actb (C28-C29, Figure 3D), Rosa26 (C30, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B-C), and Sox2 (C31, Figure 3—figure supplement 2) consistently show significant improvements. The summary conclusion (C32) is well-supported by data from all three loci, demonstrating reproducibility.

result: Farrerol treatment had no obvious negative effects on genomic stability in human fibroblasts or mouse ESCs, as assessed by γH2AX and 53BP1 immunostaining, comet assay, karyotype analysis, and DNA replication assays. In contrast, SCR7 and RS-1 showed genotoxic side effects including increased γH2AX positive cells, genomic instability, and abnormal karyotypes.
evaluation: Claims C33-C41 and C68 comprehensively assess genomic stability. Multiple independent assays (immunofluorescence in Figures 4A-D, comet assay in Figure 4E, karyotyping in Figure 4F, EdU incorporation in Figure 4—figure supplement 2) consistently show no adverse effects of farrerol while revealing problems with SCR7 and RS-1. The convergence of multiple orthogonal approaches strongly supports the safety conclusion.

result: Farrerol fully supported mouse embryo development through blastocyst hatching similar to control and RS-1, while SCR7 significantly impaired blastocyst production. Short-period treatment with all three compounds had minimal effects on early embryo development, but when DSBs were induced at the zygote stage, farrerol-treated embryos showed 82.4% blastocyst production compared to only 62.5% for SCR7.
evaluation: Claims C42-C46 assess compound effects on embryo development. Data in Figures 5A-C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C demonstrate that farrerol does not impair development while SCR7 does. The distinction between continuous treatment and short-period treatment (C44) and the effects when DSBs are induced (C45-C46) provide important context for the compound's safety and efficacy in embryos.

result: Farrerol significantly improved CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knock-in efficiency in mouse blastocysts at the Actb locus. The rate of mCherry+ blastocysts was 27.3% (0.05 μM) and 21.0% (0.1 μM) compared to 14.0% in controls, with in-frame integration rates of 27.0% and 23.0% versus 13.0% in controls. This efficiency was comparable to or higher than HMEJ (22.7%) and MMEJ (11.9%) methods, while SCR7 and RS-1 showed only slight improvements.
evaluation: Claims C47-C51 and C69 demonstrate farrerol's efficacy in blastocysts. Fluorescence data (C47, Figures 5F-G) and PCR genotyping (C50, Figure 5H) provide complementary evidence. The comparison to HMEJ/MMEJ methods (C48) and to SCR7/RS-1 (C49, C51) contextualizes the results. The data consistently support the conclusion across multiple measurement approaches.

result: Farrerol significantly improved knock-in efficiency at the Cdx2 locus in mouse embryos and enabled efficient generation of knock-in mice with germline transmission capacity. In farrerol-treated embryos, mCherry+ signals in trophectoderm increased by 57.4-68.3%, and 12 of 33 mice (36.4%) showed in-frame integration compared to only 1 of 53 in controls. The generated Cdx2-mCherry mice showed proper expression patterns at E7.5 and E9.5 and transmitted the allele to F1 offspring following Mendelian segregation.
evaluation: Claims C52-C62 and C70 demonstrate successful generation of knock-in mice. Blastocyst data (C52-C53, Figures 6B-C), founder mouse generation (C54-C56, Figure 6E), germline transmission (C57-C58, Figure 6E), homozygous line establishment (C59-C60, Figure 6F), and proper expression patterns (C61-C62, Figure 6G) provide comprehensive evidence. The complete characterization from blastocyst to F1 generation strongly supports the claims.

result: Co-injection of farrerol with CRISPR/Cas9 components into zygotes significantly increased gene editing rates at both Actb (2.3-2.6 fold) and Cdx2 (2.0-2.3 fold) loci, while co-injection of SCR7 or RS-1 had mild effects.
evaluation: Claims C63-C65 describe an alternative delivery method. Data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-D show that direct co-injection of farrerol with CRISPR components improves efficiency at both loci tested. This provides additional evidence for farrerol's efficacy and demonstrates flexibility in application methods.

result: Farrerol effectively promotes precise targeted integration in human cells, mouse cells and mouse embryos at multiple genomic loci.
evaluation: Claim C67 is a summary statement supported by the collective evidence from multiple experiments across different cell types (HEK 293FT, mouse ESCs, mouse embryos) and genomic loci (AAVS1, Actb, Rosa26, Sox2, Cdx2). This claim integrates findings from multiple result groups and is well-supported by the comprehensive dataset.
